ideas.title: Wool on the sail: trim the land yacht by its telltales
ideas.critique: The first idea in many sessions where the player does something with their hands, not a device filmed alone: a 3D solved flow that rides with the cart and yarns that read it is new physics the island never had, and trimming by eye is a real skill. The risk is that the GPU box will not re-solve fast enough to keep up with the cart. Then the threads lag the trim and the payoff turns into a canned table.

ideas.title: Hike out: the friends' weight keeps the yacht on its wheels
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Picking the crew for the wind is a real choice, and the friends finally matter by their mass, not as props. It needs a sailing cart that works before it shows anything, and if the friends 'walk to where they are called' as a scripted move, the scrambling in the film is animation, not a body.

ideas.title: The axle dynamo against the wind
ideas.critique: It is honest energy bookkeeping with one choice every run, and it is the big goal's own step. But the pitched film is one more close fixed shot of a copper motor turning, and the island has three of those already; the sparks will not hide that.

ideas.title: Sail cloth that luffs for real
ideas.critique: Two-way coupled membrane flutter in a live game is the kind of thing nobody expects from an agent, and if it works it is clip material. It hangs on a cloth contact fix that is still open and on a coupling that blows up easily, and for the player it adds sound and look to trimming more than a new goal.

ideas.title: Plank fences in Jump in: the dune drifts while you watch
ideas.critique: Shaping terrain with wind through objects you place is a real toy, and it reuses solvers the island already has. Drifts that build 'within minutes' mean the time is sped up and the saltation tuned to look right, and it sits on a side branch of the road.

ideas.title: Lumi's crest is a wind vane
ideas.nearest: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Strong for Lumi's own body and for motion, but feathers blowing in the wind is secondary animation players expect from any game, and turning away from a gust is a threshold behaviour. Nothing here gives the player a goal.

ideas.title: Beach race: each friend rigs a board sail
ideas.critique: Friends using the machines answers an old complaint, but 'Pickles too tight, Truffle luffs' is the same recipe as three variants side by side with different outcomes, given a temper. Several solved boxes at once will most likely become one shared table.

ideas.title: Tacking up the beach
ideas.critique: Pointing upwind is real sailing play that comes from apparent wind and side grip, not from a script, and the boom slamming over is a good physical beat. Treating the wheels as a keel invites a hand-tuned grip constant, and the top-down film of a track in the sand is weak to watch.

ideas.title: The wind map in the sand
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Reading the world instead of a gauge is the right instinct, but ripples are mostly a look written over hours, and a still of sand at low sun is a pretty picture with little to play.

ideas.title: Capsize
ideas.critique: Tipping over is the honest result of oversheeting, and pushing it back up together echoes the moment the big goal wants. It is much the same rigid body and heel moment as the hike-out idea, and friends tumbling off and heaving the mast will likely be the scripted part.
